1oru2l5:260: Claude Code's design philosophy is to treat "failure is inevitable" as a design premise, not an exception. The core mechanism of StreamingToolExecutor: while the model streams output, as soon as a tool_use JSON block is detected, tool execution starts immediately, without waiting for the model to finish ^. Read-only operations run in parallel, up to 10 at a time; write operations are queued serially ^. More critical is the "tombstone message" mechanism: when the API is interrupted, an error placeholder is generated for every orphaned tool call, and the interruption message is marked as TombstoneMessage, keeping the message stream intact ^. This design does not try to eliminate failure; instead, it keeps the system's state integrity and debuggability in the face of faults ^.

bn1691:221: Claude Code's memory solution is Markdown + YAML frontmatter, not a vector database ^. The underlying logic of this choice: vector matching handles lexical similarity, but it cannot compute the semantic connection between "last time we said don't mock the database" and "now we need to write database tests" ^. A small model (reasoning over 5 file headers) costs very little, yet it can capture this precise task-context association ^. The Feedback mechanism records both "corrections" and "confirmations"—learning only from mistakes makes the agent increasingly conservative; also recording what was done right prevents regression ^.
